items.text: Subscribers are the one fragile check: 0.8 per 1,000 views against a usual 1.8. DesignerTom converts at 3 per 1,000 views, Dive Club at 1.8.
items.recommendation: Add a spoken subscribe ask and a pinned chat link at the live high point this week, starting on Dive Club since it converts lower. Then see whether subscribers per 1,000 views moves on the next episode.

items.text: Search and suggested videos brought 7.6 percent of views in the latest read against a usual 14.3. Existing subscribers supply 71.4 percent of views, and search alone only 4.9 percent.
items.recommendation: Retitle the next episode and rewrite its description around the plain phrase a stranger would search for, such as portfolio review. Then compare its search and suggested share with this one.

items.text: Launches ran soft on E5 and E6: 1,127 and 1,189 YouTube views at launch against typical 1,790.5 and 1,751 for episodes around them.
items.recommendation: Post a short clip and a plain announce on both channels a few days before the next episode, and track whether launch views reach the typical first week of 1,751. Treat it as a test.

items.text: E14, only 3 days in, lost 5 of every 100 viewers about 8% of the way in, around minute 8, during a product walkthrough. It lost another 5 of every 100 later, past the halfway point. These are early-episode numbers.
items.recommendation: Test trimming the walkthrough to a short demo, or moving it after the first guest conversation. Read the early drop again on the next episode before deciding whether it mattered.

items.text: Live turnout and chat are healthy: E14 peaked at 142 viewers against a usual 97.5, with 79.6 chatters per 100 against 53.9. About a third in, 5.5 extra viewers of every 100 were watching.
items.recommendation: Keep the portfolio-review format and drop a direct chat question right around the one-third mark next episode, to protect that engagement and see if the mid-show rise repeats.
